details: CONFIRMED for the one case: the item's found_in "finding F1 of review-rules-red.json" is exactly add_from's context string
(lib/relay_queue.py:980), and add_from (976-994) reads only the review (find_finding) and never looks at stored checks or their
verdicts. The check marked F1 MET two minutes before the item was filed. PLAUSIBLE that it repeats: any LOW finding fixed
inside its change ("fixed in the change when cheap") and then queued from the review file after the merge takes the same path,
and each costs a lane, a builder and a review (here: about 20 agent minutes and one Opus review). Rated MEDIUM under
Principle 2 (waste built into the setup that repeats per change); LOW if the owner sees it as a one-off front slip.
The same item also cannot close by the cycle (Q1 can never be MET: the test passes at the take-time base), so it ends in a
manual --fixed-by close. Size: 30 agent minutes (look up checks naming the review, by relay_marks or .relay/checks, and a test).
evidence: found 2026-10-25T16:57:05Z in finding F1 of review-rules-red.json
$ git log --all -S "Base restores only four keys" --format='%h %ad %s' --date=iso
tests/relay_testbase.py:14: LOW: F1 Base restores only four keys; ...
$ git log -1 --date=iso 58d5d5f9  -> 2026-10-25 20:26:01 +0400 F1: Base restores the whole environment, not four keys
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 58d5d5f9 master && echo ANCESTOR -> ANCESTOR
failing_case: review-rules-red.json F1 (tests/relay_testbase.py:14, LOW). Commit 58d5d5f9 fixed it on wt/rules-red; the check
"Source: review-rules-red.json F1 ... Verdict: MET". At 20:57:06 (d6545df5) `relay queue add --from review-rules-red.json F1`
created base-restores-only-four-keys-bench-s-relay-claud, with Why "merged as is". Now: the item is accepted; on 28 Oct a
lane was started, a builder ran, and this review ran, for a problem that was already fixed. Should: refuse with a line such
as "F1 of review-rules-red.json is MET in the check of c73891d5 (fixed by the change): nothing to queue".
fix_hint: In add_from, before add(): look up the stored checks (relay_marks / .relay/checks) whose findings carry Source = this review
and id = fid; if any has verdict MET, raise Refused naming the check and pointing to `relay check show`. Alternatively the
front's step that queues LOW findings after a merge lists only findings not MET in the last check.
pass_cases: 1. A review JSON with finding F1, and a stored check whose findings list F1 from that review with verdict MET:
`relay queue add --from <review.json> F1 --input <toml>` is refused, the message names the check and says MET; no item file is written.
2. Same review, check records F1 NOT MET (or no check names that review): the item is created as today.
3. A review with F1 and F2, check has F1 MET, F2 NOT MET: --from F2 creates the item; --from F1 is refused.
4. A finding with kind outside (never fixed in the change, so never MET): queued as today.
reason: Outside the change (queue add --from does not check stored MET verdicts); goes to the owner as a fix item, not fixed here.
findings.summary: Principle 2 (Waste): queue add --from files a review finding that a later check of the same change already recorded MET
